summary: The corroboration audit examined 24 key details from Brendan Dassey's interrogations. Investigators introduced 12 details first, the suspect introduced 7 first, 4 were already public before interviews, and 1 may trace to an earlier unrecorded statement. One detail raised by investigators was never adopted. The three recorded sessions show high interrogator word share (68–92%), hundreds of fact-carrying questions, and frequent use of "we already know," minimization, and demand-truth tactics.
key_points: 12 details were first stated by investigators before the suspect adopted them (e.g., vehicle in garage p. fassbender; knife p. wiegert; body in RAV4 p. fassbender; stabbed in stomach p. fassbender; hair cut p. wiegert; shot in head p. wiegert; shot in garage p. wiegert; RAV4 hidden p. fassbender; license plates removed p. wiegert; Avery raised hood p. wiegert; blood on garage floor p. wiegert; phone/camera/purse burned p. wiegert; bones broken up p. fassbender).

7 details originated with the suspect in the record (tied up with rope p. brendan; restrained on bed p. brendan; strangled p. brendan; throat cut p. brendan; shot with .22 rifle p. brendan; tires/branches on fire p. brendan; bedsheets burned p. brendan).

4 details were publicly reported before any interview (body burned behind garage public Nov 16, 2005 p. brendan/fassbender; license plates removed public Nov 16, 2005 p. brendan/wiegert; vehicle key in bedroom public Nov 10, 2005 p. brendan; clothes burned public Nov 16, 2005 p. brendan).
1 detail (bleach on jeans) may trace to an earlier unrecorded statement with no public transcript (Decision and Order p. 7, citing ECF 19-19 at 10-11).
1 detail (tattoo on stomach) was raised by investigators but never adopted by the suspect (p. fassbender).

Across three recorded sessions, interrogators spoke 68–92% of words, asked 305–1154 questions with 91–366 carrying facts, and used "we already know" (52 total), minimization (30), and demand-truth (85) tactics (Sessions S1, S2, S3).
limits: This audit cannot determine whether adopted details reflect actual knowledge or compliance with suggestion.
It does not assess the voluntariness or reliability of the suspect's statements.
Transcripts for two sessions (S1b, S1c) are unavailable, leaving gaps in the disclosure sequence.
Public reporting dates are taken from the provided record; independent media verification is not included.
